title: basic-auth fail-closed backstop: only response filters authorize a route on their own; ownership grants and cleanups do not
answers: Why can a user without a workspace create grant still create a gateway secret in the basic-auth server?
A route has an after-request ownership grant but no before-request validator. Is it blocked by the fail-closed check?
Where does the auth server decide whether a route without a before-request validator is allowed through?
I'm adding a new response filter for a list route. Do I need to register it somewhere so the fail-closed check accepts it?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_authorized_outside_before_request is the fail-closed backstop for routes that have no before-request validator. It is consulted for every request in the basic-auth app, including gateway secret, experiment and registered-model create and list routes.
Rule: A route counts as self-authorizing only if its AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS entry is in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS (the filter_* and redact_* response handlers). Ownership grants (set_can_manage_*) and permission cleanups (for example _cleanup_workspace_permissions) run after an already-authorized write, so they must not exempt a route. Every route that carries a set_can_manage_* grant must have a before-request validator registered in the before-request map; mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_create_gateway_secret is the example added for CreateGatewaySecret.
Symptom: With workspaces enabled, a user denied CreateExperiment and CreateRegisteredModel could still create gateway secrets, because the MANAGE grant handler silently satisfied the backstop and no create check ran.
Constraints: Applies to routes gated by before-request validators and response filters. When you add a new response filter, add it to _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS; a new ownership grant needs its own before-request validator, not a filter entry. tests/server/auth/test_authorization_coverage.py:test_every_ownership_grant_route_has_a_before_request_validator fails if a grant route lacks a validator; tests/server/auth/test_fail_closed_flag.py:test_ownership_grant_after_handler_does_not_authorize_route covers the backstop itself.
applies: Basic-auth server (mlflow/server/auth) request authorization for any route with an AFTER_REQUEST handler; not for the content of individual validators.
says: A user without permission to create workspace items can still add gateway secrets.
Restricted team members can unexpectedly save AI gateway connection credentials in locked workspaces.
Prevent users who lack workspace creation access from adding new gateway secrets.
Users blocked from creating experiments can still configure gateway credentials in the workspace.
search: In the basic-auth server, mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_authorized_outside_before_request acts as the fail-closed backstop for routes without a before-request validator by authorizing only handlers listed in _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS. Ownership grants like set_can_manage_* and cleanup handlers do not authorize a route on their own and require a dedicated before-request validator such as validate_can_create_gateway_secret. New response filters must be registered in _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS, as checked by tests/server/auth/test_authorization_coverage.py:test_every_ownership_grant_route_has_a_before_request_validator and tests/server/auth/test_fail_closed_flag.py:test_ownership_grant_after_handler_does_not_authorize_route.
